problem: No document says how landed work reaches a remote. The Overseer never pushes: a landing is a local fast-forward of the main checkout. Nothing tells User to push, when it is safe, or that a push or fetch during a run fails live jobs.
evidence: `src/` holds `push` only as a denied git subcommand (`src/services/overseer/WorkerProfiles.ts`, `WORKER_DENIED_GIT_SUBCOMMANDS`), and no `fetch` or `pull` appears anywhere in `src/` or `cli/`. Over `docs/**/*.md`, a case-insensitive grep for `\bpush` finds only that confinement table row and an unrelated word in `measurement.md`. README, concepts, getting-started, running-a-board, runbook and airlocks-and-groups never name it. `takeRefSnapshot` in `src/lib/git/RefSnapshot.ts` snapshots every ref through `for-each-ref`, and `onlyOwnRefsMoved` in `src/services/lifecycle/Customs.ts` exempts only `refs/heads/...` and recorded landings. A `git push` updates `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` locally, so it trips V14 `foreign-ref-moved` as a `git fetch` does. `gap-outside-ref-move-fails-job` names fetch and hand commits, not push, and an operator never reaches it from a daily routine.
fix: Add a daily routine under `## Daily routines`, 'Push what landed': nothing leaves the machine unless User pushes; push from the main checkout only when `forge jobs` lists no build or review job, or accept that live jobs fail with `foreign-ref-moved` and count a failed pass; link gap-outside-ref-move-fails-job. Hand-backs for the integration pass: widen that gap entry to name `git push`, and add a line to the README's 'What it does to a repository'.

problem: Nothing says what a ticket's `type` changes. A reader filing a `research` ticket cannot learn that it runs the same build, Customs, gate, review and Airlock path as code, must produce a commit, and has no separate place for its answer.
evidence: `research` appears in code only in `TICKET_TYPES`, the `TicketType` union and the Bridge's `TICKET_TYPE_CHIPS`. The only behaviour keyed on `type` is `bug`: `src/lib/tracker-model/TicketLinks.ts` (`introduced-by-on-a-non-bug`) and `src/lib/tracker-model/ReviewStatistics.ts`. `review-stats` also splits by type. V3 `aCommitSinceTheStart` holds a `built` report to a new commit whatever the type, so a question answered only in the Handoff goes red with `no-commit-since-start`. The docs only list the values: `docs/cli.md` 'Types are `ticket`, `bug` and `research`'. The Variants section of `ticket-lifecycle.md`, `entities.md` and the glossary are silent. `skills/agent-po/SKILL.md` says only `research` is 'a question to settle'.
fix: Add a variant under `## Variants`: the three types share one lifecycle; `type` affects only `introducedBy` legality and the review-stats `byType` split; a `research` ticket owes a commit like any other, so its finding must land as a file on the branch, and the `## Handoff` alone earns `no-commit-since-start`. Link V3 in Customs and gates.

problem: The rule that decides how many code lines a review reworked is documented nowhere. That count is compared with `REWORK_ROUND_THRESHOLD_LINES`, grants or refuses another review round and raises `rounds-not-converging`, yet no document says what counts as a code line.
evidence: `src/shared/rework/utils/ReworkCountUtil.ts` classifies each changed line as code, comment, blank or documentation. Reworked lines are added plus removed code lines (`totals.reworkedCodeLines = totals.addedCodeLines + totals.removedCodeLines`). `src/shared/rework/constants/CommentSyntaxes.ts` treats repository-rooted `docs/` and `md`, `mdx`, `rst`, `txt` as documentation, and a file type it does not list has every non-blank line counted as code. Each side of a hunk is classified in its own context, including a hunk that starts inside a block comment. The docs say only 'counts reworked code lines' (`build-and-review.md`), 'code lines only' (`measurement.md`) and the glossary's `rework`. A grep of `docs/` for `CommentSyntax`, `COMMENT_SYNTAX`, `DOCUMENTATION_EXTENSIONS` and `DOCUMENTATION_DIRECTORY` finds only one stale-prose row in known-gaps.
fix: Under `### Round verdicts` state the counting rule in a small table: what a reworked line is, so a changed line counts twice; which paths are documentation; that comments and blanks are out; that an unlisted file type counts every non-blank line, so a file type is no way under the threshold. Cite `ReworkCountUtil.reworkOfFile` and `src/shared/rework/constants/CommentSyntaxes.ts`. Link it from `measurement.md`.

problem: The rules for keeping this documentation set correct have no home in the repository. They live only in the owner's git-ignored evidence folder. A contributor learns about figures, glossary headings, wrapping and retired names, and nothing about document shape, fact ownership, defects, numbers or commit stamps. Nothing tells them the labs hold their own copy of the facts.
evidence: `style-guide.md` and `figure-conventions.md` sit under the main checkout's `.claude/.evidence/group-docs/plan/`, and no tracked doc names them. 'Changing the documentation' in `contributing.md` covers one line of 'one home', figures, glossary terms, wrap and `RETIRED_NAMES`. It does not cover: the skeleton every document follows (blockquote of Question/Time/Read first/Next, `## In one screen`, `## Invariants`, `## In the code`); which document owns which fact; the `> **As built.**` link rule and how to add a `gap-` entry; the `CONSTANT_NAME` (value) rule; or the 28 lines stamped `70ce56de`. `docs/interactive/state-explorer.html` carries a hand-written `MODEL` object, and `guards-and-testing.md` 'What specs require of docs' lists four specs, none reading a lab's facts, so a Playbook change leaves the labs silently stale.

problem: This page does not share the shell of the other three labs. It looks and reads as a different site.
evidence: failure-lab, state-explorer and why-not-moving use `.wrap`, a `.topbar` with `#crumbs` joined by a '/' separator, a `.segmented` lowercase theme control, and the tokens `--surface/--raised/--text`. ticket-journey uses `.page` (max-width 1240px, padding 20px 24px), a `fieldset.theme` with a visible 'Theme' legend and separate capitalised buttons, and crumbs with no separator. It also has its own tokens: `--page`, `--surface` as the card colour, `--ink`, `--mono`. Its light values differ too: `--hairline` #E4DFD2 against #ECE7DC, muted #5F5E5A against #62615B. The 1280 screenshots show the difference at once.
fix: Port the shell from failure-lab.html: `.wrap`, topbar, crumbs with separator, segmented light/dark/auto control, and the shared token names and values. Keep the page's own stepper and step content, and rename the tokens its CSS uses.

problem: The theme control runs in a different order from the other labs, and the choice does not carry between pages.

problem: The page can give a wrong verdict for a board state that really occurs. An in-progress ticket with failed passes, and 'An earlier build job ran' unticked, reads as stuck when the Playbook would launch a rebuild.
evidence: I compared `stepsForThisTicket` with the real `Playbook.nextStepsOf` over 300,000 random states; the steps agreed apart from harness artefacts and this case. With status in-progress, no job, failed passes 1, replaced 0 or 1 and `earlierBuild` false, the page gives no step and the verdict 'in-progress with no job and no earlier build'. A failed pass or a `replaced` ending needs a launched job, so `candidateOf` in Playbook.ts returns `rebuild` and steps `launch-build`. `normalised()` already forces `earlierBuild` for `reviewResumesSpent`, but not for `failedPasses` or `replacedInARow`.
fix: In `normalised()`: `if (next.reviewResumesSpent || next.failedPasses > 0 || next.replacedInARow > 0) next.earlierBuild = true;`.

problem: The MODEL lists a constant that does not exist under the source it names, so a reviewer cannot compare it with the code.

Playbook.ts inlines `incident.kind === 'system-question' || incident.kind === 'malformed-ticket'` inside `jobAwaitsAnAnswer`. The other keys in that block are real constants: `PRIORITY_RANK`, `WORK_PHASE_RANK`, `TICKET_HOLDING_DECISION_KINDS`, `SLOT_TAKING_JOB_KINDS`.
fix: Rename the key so it is not a code-style constant, for example `questionLikeIncidentKinds`, and add a short note that it is transcribed from the condition in `jobAwaitsAnAnswer`.
